commands.description: Register a slash command (/ command) on the current bound Open Platform app; --force converts a name collision into an update (idempotent re-run)
commands.details:
Register a slash command (/ command) on the current bound Open Platform app; --force converts a name collision into an update (idempotent re-run)

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Use this for a new command name. On a name collision, update the existing command only when that is the user's intent.

Avoid when:
  • The command already exists and the user wants to edit it → use `+slash-command-update`.

Tips:
  • Changes may take about five minutes to appear in clients because of client-side caching; the server updates immediately.

Examples:
  • Create a localized slash command
      lark-cli application +slash-command-create --command greet --description "say hi" --description-i18n zh_cn=问候

Usage:
  lark-cli application +slash-command-create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                      identity type: bot | user
      --command string                 command name WITHOUT the leading slash (server enforces uniqueness per app; max 100 commands)
      --description string             default description shown in the client command panel (description.default_value)
      --description-i18n stringArray   localized description, repeatable, format <lang>=<text> (e.g. zh_cn=发送问候); language codes are passed through to the server
      --dry-run                        print request without executing
      --force                          on name collision, resolve the existing command by name and update it in place
      --format string                  output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                           help for +slash-command-create
      --icon-key string                icon key (server default: skill_outlined; invalid keys are rejected server-side with code 40000031)
  -q, --jq string                      jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                           shorthand for --format json

command.description: command name WITHOUT the leading slash (server enforces uniqueness per app; max 100 commands)

description.description: default description shown in the client command panel (description.default_value)

description-i18n.description: localized description, repeatable, format <lang>=<text> (e.g. zh_cn=发送问候); language codes are passed through to the server

force.description: on name collision, resolve the existing command by name and update it in place

icon-key.description: icon key (server default: skill_outlined; invalid keys are rejected server-side with code 40000031)

commands.description: Delete a slash command from the current bound app (high-risk: irreversible; recreating the same name yields a new command_id)
commands.details:
Delete a slash command from the current bound app (high-risk: irreversible; recreating the same name yields a new command_id)

Risk: high-risk-write (requires explicit user confirmation to execute; the agent must NOT add --yes on its own — only pass --yes after the user has confirmed)

When to use:
  • Use this only after the user explicitly confirms the target and the irreversible deletion.

Prerequisites:
  • Explicit user confirmation is required before passing `--yes`; an agent must not self-approve the deletion.
  • Pass `--command-id` from `+slash-command-list`, or pass `--command` to let the CLI resolve the current id by name with a live list request.

Tips:
  • Deleted commands may linger in clients for about five minutes because of client-side caching.
  • Recreating the same command name produces a new `command_id`.

Examples:
  • Delete by name after explicit user confirmation
      lark-cli application +slash-command-delete --command greet --yes

Usage:
  lark-cli application +slash-command-delete [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: bot | user
      --command string      target command name WITHOUT leading slash (resolved via live list, needs read scope); mutually exclusive with --command-id
      --command-id string   target command_id; mutually exclusive with --command
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +slash-command-delete
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                shorthand for --format json
      --yes                 confirm high-risk operation

command.description: target command name WITHOUT leading slash (resolved via live list, needs read scope); mutually exclusive with --command-id

commands.description: Update description / localized descriptions / icon of a slash command on the current bound app, addressed by --command-id or by name via --command
commands.details:
Update description / localized descriptions / icon of a slash command on the current bound app, addressed by --command-id or by name via --command

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Use this to change description, localized descriptions, or icon while retaining the command name and `command_id`.

Prerequisites:
  • Pass `--command-id` from `+slash-command-list`, or pass `--command` to let the CLI resolve the current id by name with a live list request.

Tips:
  • PATCH is field-level partial: fields you do not pass are preserved server-side.
  • The command name cannot be changed. Renaming means deleting and recreating the command, which produces a new `command_id`.

Examples:
  • Update by name (the CLI resolves the current command id first)
      lark-cli application +slash-command-update --command greet --description "new text"

Usage:
  lark-cli application +slash-command-update [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                      identity type: bot | user
      --command string                 target command name WITHOUT leading slash; resolved via live list (needs read scope); mutually exclusive with --command-id
      --command-id string              target command_id (from +slash-command-list or create output); mutually exclusive with --command
      --description string             new default description (description.default_value)
      --description-i18n stringArray   localized description, repeatable <lang>=<text>; REPLACES the whole i18n map (missing languages are dropped); requires --description
      --dry-run                        print request without executing
      --format string                  output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                           help for +slash-command-update
      --icon-key string                new icon key (invalid keys rejected server-side with code 40000031)
  -q, --jq string                      jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                           shorthand for --format json

API Parameters:
  Required:
      --employee-type string   Employee ID type. If you don't have background administrative privileges, you can use Get user ID by mobile phone number or email. enum: employee_id=Employee's employee ID, that is the user ID in Feishu Admin > Organization > Member and Department > Member Details|employee_no=Employee number, that is the employee number shown in Feishu Admin > Organization > Members and Departments > Member details
  Optional:
      --ignore-invalid-users      Whether to ignore invalid and no permissions users, the corresponding employee_type. If true, return the information of the valid user and inform the invalid and no permissions user. bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)

If true, return the data of all current + departing employees corresponding to employee_no/employee_id. bool flag (presence = true; omit for false; takes no value)

Request Body:
      --data string   JSON request body. Supports - and @file.

Raw Parameter Input:
      --params string   Raw URL/query params JSON. Supports - and @file. If both set, typed flags override matching keys in --params.

Execution:
      --as string   identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run     print request without executing

Output:
      --format string   output format: json|ndjson|table|csv (default json)
  -q, --jq string       jq expression to filter JSON output
  -o, --output string   output file path for binary responses

Other:
  -h, --help   help for query
      --json   shorthand for --format json

employee_type.description: Employee ID type. If you don't have background administrative privileges, you can use Get user ID by mobile phone number or email
enumDescriptions: Employee's employee ID, that is the user ID in Feishu Admin > Organization > Member and Department > Member Details
Employee number, that is the employee number shown in Feishu Admin > Organization > Members and Departments > Member details

ignore_invalid_users.description: Whether to ignore invalid and no permissions users, the corresponding employee_type. If true, return the information of the valid user and inform the invalid and no permissions user; if false, and there are invalid or no permissions in the user_ids, return an error

include_terminated_user.description: Since the new employee can reuse the employee_no/employee_id of the departed employee, corresponding to employee_type. If true, return the data of all current + departing employees corresponding to employee_no/employee_id; if false, only return the data of the current or most recent employee corresponding to employee_no/employee_id

check_date_from.description: The starting working day of the query, in the format yyyyMMdd

check_date_to.description: The closing working day of the query, in the format yyyyMMdd

need_overtime_result.description: Whether you need the overtime shift clock in result; when need_overtime_result = true, the overtime shift will be returned. The overtime shift is marked by task_shift_type = 1, and there will be shared record_id when the overtime shift is connected to the normal shift. For example: 9-18 is the normal shift, 18-19 is the overtime shift, and the clock in result records two segments, 9-18, 18-19 and the two segments record_id the same (check_in_record_id and check_out_record_id are the same). Non-connected overtime shifts are returned in normal segments. When need_overtime_result = false, only the normal shift is returned and task_shift_type = 0

user_ids.description: employee_no or employee_id list, corresponding to employee_type, not more than 50 in length

commands.description: Create a block on a BaseApp page
commands.details:
Create a block on a BaseApp page

Usage:
  lark-cli base +app-block-create [flags]

Flags:
      --app-token string     BaseApp token
      --as string            identity type: user | bot
      --data-config string   data_config JSON object; read lark-base-app-block-data-config.md for the SSOT
      --dry-run              print request without executing
      --format string        output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                 help for +app-block-create
  -q, --jq string            jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                 shorthand for --format json
      --name string          block name
      --no-validate          skip local data_config validation and normalization; send data_config as-is
      --page-id string       BaseApp page ID
      --sub-type string      list subtype: standard|grouped|collapsible|card|detail; defaults to standard (standard|grouped|collapsible|card|detail)
      --type string          block type: chart(column|bar|line|pie|ring|area|combo|scatter|funnel|wordCloud|radar|statistics) | text | list. Read lark-base-app-block-data-config.md before creating. (column|bar|line|pie|ring|scatter|funnel|wordCloud|area|combo|radar|statistics|text|list)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Order Count" --type statistics --data-config '{"base_token":"basxxx","data_sources":[{"table_name":"Orders","count_all":true}]}'
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Monthly sales" --type column --data-config '{"base_token":"basxxx","data_sources":[{"table_name":"Orders","series":[{"field_name":"Amount","rollup":"SUM"}],"group_by":[{"field_name":"Month","sort":{"type":"group","order":"asc"}}]}]}'
    • Chart blocks use multi-datasource data_config: one top-level base_token shared by all sources, with table_name/series/count_all/group_by/filter inside each data_sources[] element (text needs none). App block commands carry no --base-token.
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Notes" --type text --data-config '{"text":"# Sales overview"}'
    • lark-cli base +app-block-create --app-token <app_token> --page-id <page_id> --name "Open orders" --type list --sub-type standard --data-config '{"base_token":"basxxx","table_name":"Orders"}'
    • For list creates, omit optional columns/fields to use the product defaults. The CLI sends them only when explicitly provided.
    • Before creating data-backed blocks, use +table-list and +field-list to confirm real table and field names.
    • A list accepts exactly one base_token, and that Base must be in the same Workspace as the App.
    • Read lark-base-app-block-data-config.md as the SSOT for chart, list and text config; do not invent data_config from natural language.
    • Block type cannot be changed after creation and this phase has no delete command, so a wrong --type can only be fixed in the UI. Confirm the type before creating.
    • Widget layout, position, size and display settings are not part of the public create/update protocol; the platform applies product defaults.
    • Record block_id for +app-block-update. For chart data reads, pass the returned chart_token to +app-block-get-data --block-id.
    • Block names must be unique within the page; the CLI checks every existing block before creation.
    • Create blocks sequentially; do not parallelize multiple block creates for the same page.

type.description: block type: chart(column|bar|line|pie|ring|area|combo|scatter|funnel|wordCloud|radar|statistics) | text | list. Read lark-base-app-block-data-config.md before creating. (column|bar|line|pie|ring|scatter|funnel|wordCloud|area|combo|radar|statistics|text|list)

commands.description: Create a block in a dashboard
commands.details:
Create a block in a dashboard

Usage:
  lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --base-token string     base token
      --dashboard-id string   dashboard ID

  -h, --help                  help for +dashboard-block-create
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --name string           block name
      --no-validate           skip local SEMANTIC validation: data_config checks + normalization, and the --position x/y/w/h completeness check. JSON syntax is still parsed (a malformed value never silently vanishes from the preview). Sends data_config and position as-is
      --position string       optional. component position+size in 12-col grid, JSON {"x","y","w","h"}; all four keys required and numeric (position is submitted whole, so a partial object cannot express a complete placement). Advisory bounds x/y>=0, 1<=w<=12 and x+w<=12, h>=1 — coordinate VALUES are not validated locally and pass through as given; the server auto-arranges out-of-range or overlapping positions. Omit for server auto-layout
      --type string           block type: column(柱状图)|bar(条形图)|line(折线图)|pie(饼图)|ring(环形图)|area(面积图)|combo(组合图)|scatter(散点图)|funnel(漏斗图)|wordCloud(词云)|radar(雷达图)|ranking(排行榜)|statistics(指标卡)|text(文本). Read lark-base-dashboard-block-config.md before creating.
      --user-id-type string   user ID type for user fields in filters: open_id / union_id / user_id

Risk: write

Tips:
    • lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --base-token <base_token> --dashboard-id <dashboard_id> --name "Order Count" --type statistics --data-config '{"table_name":"Orders","count_all":true}'
    • lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --base-token <base_token> --dashboard-id <dashboard_id> --name "Revenue" --type statistics --data-config '{"table_name":"Orders","series":[{"field_name":"Amount","rollup":"SUM"}],"number_format":{"formatName":"dollar_rounded","precision":2}}'
    • lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --base-token <base_token> --dashboard-id <dashboard_id> --name "Top Owners" --type ranking --data-config '{"table_name":"Orders","group_by":[{"field_name":"Owner"}],"series":[{"field_name":"Amount","rollup":"SUM"}]}'
    • lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --base-token <base_token> --dashboard-id <dashboard_id> --name "Dashboard Note" --type text --data-config '{"text":"# Sales Dashboard"}'
    • lark-cli base +dashboard-block-create --base-token <base_token> --dashboard-id <dashboard_id> --name "Order Count" --type statistics --data-config '{"table_name":"Orders","count_all":true}' --position '{"x":0,"y":0,"w":6,"h":4}'
    • Before creating data-backed blocks, use +table-list and +field-list to confirm real table and field names.
    • data_config uses table and field names, not table_id or field_id.
    • Read lark-base-dashboard-block-config.md as the SSOT for chart templates, filters, metric rules, and type-specific fields; do not invent data_config from natural language.
    • --position is optional precise layout in a 12-col grid; omit it to let the server auto-layout. Coordinate values are not validated locally; the server auto-arranges out-of-range or overlapping positions. To re-tidy an existing dashboard use +dashboard-arrange instead.
    • For funnel/stage charts backed by ordered helper data, set the intended group_by.sort in the initial create request; do not create first and then issue a second update just to fix sorting.
    • Record the returned block_id; block update/delete/get-data commands need it.
    • Create dashboard blocks sequentially; do not parallelize multiple block creates for the same dashboard.

Flags:

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Example text: lark-cli base +field-create --base-token <base_token> --table-id <table_id> --json '{"name":"Status","type":"text"}'
    • Example select: lark-cli base +field-create --base-token <base_token> --table-id <table_id> --json '{"name":"Status","type":"select","multiple":false,"options":[{"name":"Todo"},{"name":"Done"}]}'
    • +field-create defines storage schema only: choose a documented field type from explicit stored-value requirements and the user's semantics. Treat the field name or business purpose only as a clue to confirm; do not use it to invent derived behavior. Use style only to format the chosen type.
    • For explicitly requested derived, automatic, synchronized, or backfilled behavior, use documented formula, lookup, link, workflow, or automation only. If unsupported, do not probe code/web/OpenAPI, create a storage placeholder, or claim completion; report the boundary and alternatives.
    • Agent hint: for multiple fields in one table, prefer one array; array items are created sequentially.
    • For generated arrays, prefer --json @file or an argv-safe subprocess call; do not double-escape JSON inside shell command substitution.
    • For large arrays, bound successful stdout with --jq 'if .ok then (.data | {created,total,field_get_recommended,next_step,verification_hint}) else . end'; this preserves the full partial-failure envelope. Omit the projection when individual field IDs are needed.
    • On successful simple fields, next_step:done means stop: do not list/get fields unless readback is explicitly requested; if needed, filter +field-list with --jq instead of printing every field.

Batch create records

Usage:

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user | bot

      --table-id string     table ID (must start with tbl if ID) or name

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Happy path field: create_records is an array of independent record field maps.
    • Example: {"create_records":[{"Name":"Task A","Status":["Todo"]},{"Name":"Task B","Score":20}]}.
    • Before writing, use +field-list to confirm real writable fields; do not write system fields, formula, lookup, or attachment fields as normal CellValue.
    • Batch create supports max 200 records per call.
    • After batch-creating known helper rows, use the returned record IDs and your submitted rows; do not immediately +record-list the same table unless you need server-normalized formula/lookup values or failure diagnosis.
    • Use the record-batch-create guide for command limits and edge cases.
    • CellValue happy path: text/phone/url -> "text"; number/currency/percent/rating -> 12.5; select -> ["Todo"] or ["Tag A","Tag B"] (when multiple=false, the array can contain only one option); datetime -> "2026-03-24 10:00"; checkbox -> true/false.
    • ID-based CellValue: user/group/link fields use arrays like [{"id":"ou_xxx"}], [{"id":"oc_xxx"}], [{"id":"rec_xxx"}]; location uses {"lng":116.397428,"lat":39.90923}; null clears a cell when allowed.
    • User and group fields always use arrays; when multiple=false, the array can contain only one item.
    • Do not guess user/chat/linked-record IDs or location coordinates; resolve them first with the relevant contact/im/record lookup flow.
    • Use lark-base-cell-value.md for complex CellValue shapes and special field types; do not invent values for fields not covered by the happy path.

    • Use +record-search flag mode for keyword matching; combine --filter-json or --sort-json to narrow or order matches. For filter/sort-only reads, use +record-list.
    • Use --json only when you need to pass the full search body directly.
    • If file I/O is available, prefer --format ndjson --output ./records.ndjson for analysis, parsing, or comparison to keep long user data out of model context; process the records file with Python or another data analysis engine. Follow lark-base-record-query-and-analysis-sop.md for engine selection and complete-data checks. Ndjson defaults to limit 2000, so set a smaller --limit only for probes, previews, or an explicitly bounded result.

commands.description: Create or update a record
commands.details:
Create or update a record

Usage:
  lark-cli base +record-upsert [flags]

Flags:
      --as string           identity type: user | bot
      --base-token string   base token
      --dry-run             print request without executing
      --format string       output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                help for +record-upsert
  -q, --jq string           jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json string         record field map JSON object, e.g. {"Name":"Alice","Status":["Todo"]}; do not wrap in fields
      --record-id string    record ID
      --table-id string     table ID (must start with tbl if ID) or name

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Happy path JSON is a top-level field map: each key is a real field name or field ID, each value is that field's CellValue.
    • Without --record-id this creates a record; with --record-id this updates that record. It does not auto-upsert by business key.
    • Before writing, use +field-list to confirm real writable fields; do not write system fields, formula, lookup, or attachment fields as normal CellValue.
    • Sub-record/child-record path: when a one-way/two-way link field represents hierarchy, create a normal record and set that link field to a parent record reference array, e.g. {"Parent Link":[{"id":"rec_xxx"}]}; do not look for parent_record_id or a separate child-record API.
    • CellValue happy path: text/phone/url -> "text"; number/currency/percent/rating -> 12.5; select -> ["Todo"] or ["Tag A","Tag B"] (when multiple=false, the array can contain only one option); datetime -> "2026-03-24 10:00"; checkbox -> true/false.
    • ID-based CellValue: user/group/link fields use arrays like [{"id":"ou_xxx"}], [{"id":"oc_xxx"}], [{"id":"rec_xxx"}]; location uses {"lng":116.397428,"lat":39.90923}; null clears a cell when allowed.
    • User and group fields always use arrays; when multiple=false, the array can contain only one item.
    • Do not guess user/chat/linked-record IDs or location coordinates; resolve them first with the relevant contact/im/record lookup flow.
    • Use lark-base-cell-value.md for complex CellValue shapes and special field types; do not invent values for fields not covered by the happy path.

commands.description: Query free/busy for one or more users. Merges overlapping busy intervals and supports per-user free / common-free views for multi-user scheduling.
commands.details:
Query free/busy for one or more users. Merges overlapping busy intervals and supports per-user free / common-free views for multi-user scheduling.

Usage:
  lark-cli calendar +freebusy [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --end string            end time (ISO 8601, default: end of start day)
      --format string         output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                  help for +freebusy
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --min-duration string   minimum length for free/common_free candidates (Go duration, e.g. 30m, 1h); ignored for busy / raw_busy
      --start string          start time (ISO 8601, default: today)
      --type string           output view: busy (default, per-user merged busy) | raw_busy (per-user upstream events with rsvp_status) | free (per-user free windows) | common_free (all-users common free) (busy|raw_busy|free|common_free) (default "busy")
      --user-id strings       target user open_id(s); repeatable or comma-separated; default: current user; bot identity must provide at least one

Risk: read

Tips:
    • `--type busy` merges adjacent busy intervals, so item count != event count. For events/rsvp use `--type raw_busy` (own or others' calendars); for own attendees/details use `+get` / `+list-attendees`.
    • Multi-user scheduling raw view: use `--type common_free --min-duration <dur>` and let the CLI compute the intersection instead of merging by hand.

end.description: end time (ISO 8601, default: end of start day)

commands.details:
Transfer the organizer role of a calendar event to another user or bot

Usage:
  lark-cli calendar +transfer [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                   identity type: user | bot
      --calendar-id string          calendar ID the event lives on (default: primary)
      --dry-run                     print request without executing
      --event-id string             event ID to transfer (uid_originalTime)
      --format string               output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                        help for +transfer
  -q, --jq string                   jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                        shorthand for --format json
      --remove-original-organizer   remove the original organizer instead of keeping them as an attendee; the server forces this on a shared calendar, where original_organizer_removed is omitted from the result
      --to-user-id string           receiver open_id (ou_...); becomes the new organizer. May be a user or a bot
      --transfer-series             confirm transferring the entire recurring series; required for recurring events because a single occurrence cannot be transferred
      --yes                         confirm high-risk operation

Risk: high-risk-write

Tips:
    • Transferring is irreversible and also moves meeting minutes, notes and attachments to the new organizer; pass --yes to confirm.
    • --as must be the event's current organizer (user or bot); --to-user-id may be a user or a bot, so all four user/bot directions are expressed by those two flags.
    • Example: lark-cli calendar +transfer --event-id <uid_originalTime> --to-user-id ou_xxx --yes

commands.description: Update a calendar event and incrementally add or remove attendees
commands.details:
Update a calendar event and incrementally add or remove attendees Usage: lark-cli calendar +update [flags] Flags: --add-attendee-ids string attendee IDs to add, comma-separated (supports user ou_, chat oc_, room omm_) --apply-to string recurring scope: single (this occurrence / exception only) | all (whole series and every exception) | this-and-following (truncate the series at this instance and create a new series carrying the requested edits). Required on recurring events; ignored on non-recurring events. (single|all|this-and-following) --as string identity type: user | bot --calendar-id string calendar ID (default: primary) --description # event description as Markdown (@file or - for stdin); the unified description field. Supports bold/italic/underline/strikethrough, links, headings (#..`###`), blockquotes (`>`), ordered/unordered lists, horizontal rules (`---`), GFM tables, and images (`![name](url)`; a remote URL is used as-is, and a local image path relative to and inside the current working directory is auto-uploaded to Lark drive and rendered inline — absolute/out-of-cwd paths are rejected). A Lark doc URL (bare or as a Markdown link) is auto-resolved to an inline doc-mention chip showing its title. Inside a GFM table cell, stack multiple lines with `
`; each line may itself be an ordered/unordered list item, image or styled text (e.g. `1. a
2. b`, `- x
- y`, `![p](url)
**bold**`). Passing an empty string clears the description. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others)) --dry-run print request without executing --end string new end time (ISO 8601); requires --start --event-id string event ID to update --format string output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json") -h, --help help for +update -q, --jq string jq expression to filter JSON output --json shorthand for --format json --notify send update notification to attendees (default true) --remove-attendee-ids string attendee IDs to remove, comma-separated (supports user ou_, chat oc_, room omm_) --rrule string recurrence rule (rfc5545) --start string new start time (ISO 8601); requires --end --summary string event title Risk: write

Required on recurring events; ignored on non-recurring events. (single|all|this-and-following)

Search bots (apps) by keyword — across the tenant, or inside specific chats (requires --as user)

Risk: read

When to use:
  • Search bots (apps) by keyword. Pass `--query` or `--queries`; use `--chat-ids` to search within specific chats.

Avoid when:
  • Looking for a person rather than a bot → use `+search-user`
  • Running as a bot — this shortcut is user-only

Tips:
  • `has_more=true` means the search is incomplete; refine the keyword or search scope instead of paginating

Examples:
  • Find bots by keyword
      lark-cli contact +search-bot --query "会议助手" --as user
  • Search inside one chat
      lark-cli contact +search-bot --query "助手" --chat-ids "oc_3a8b****6a7b" --as user
  • Find bots you've chatted with
      lark-cli contact +search-bot --query "助手" --has-chatted --as user
  • Search several bot keywords in one call
      lark-cli contact +search-bot --queries "会议助手,日报助手,审批助手" --as user

commands.description: Search Lark/Feishu users by keyword, open_id list, or filter (requires --as user)
commands.details:
Search Lark/Feishu users by keyword, open_id list, or filter (requires --as user)

Risk: read

When to use:
  • The primary user lookup for user identity: search by keyword or email, resolve known ids with --user-ids, or get yourself with --user-ids me — it does by-id reads too, so as a user you rarely need `+get-user`. Each match returns an open_id and p2p_chat_id to chain into follow-ups.

Avoid when:
  • Running as a bot — this shortcut is user-only; use `+get-user` instead (it supports bot identity)
  • You only need users' personal status for ids you already hold → use `user_profiles batch_query`

Tips:
  • Filter-only enumeration — users you've chatted with: lark-cli contact +search-user --has-chatted
  • Refine same-name hits: lark-cli contact +search-user --query '张三' --has-chatted --exclude-external-users
  • Multi-name fanout: lark-cli contact +search-user --queries 'alice,bob,张三'
  • on has_more=true add filters or tighten --query — there is no auto-pagination.

Examples:
  • Find a user by name
      lark-cli contact +search-user --query "alice" --as user
  • Fetch known users by open_id (me = yourself)
      lark-cli contact +search-user --user-ids "ou_3a8b****6a7b,me" --as user

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Create a new Lark document from DocxXML or Markdown, optionally in a folder or Wiki node.

commands.description: Update a Lark document
commands.details:
Update a Lark document

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Apply targeted text or block edits, append content, or deliberately replace an entire Lark document.

Tips:
  • Prefer `str_replace` or `block_*` commands for targeted edits. Use `overwrite` only when replacing the entire document is intended; it can discard unrelated rich content.
  • Before a `block_*` edit, fetch the target with `lark-cli docs +fetch --detail with-ids` and a narrow `--scope`; refetch after structural changes before reusing block IDs.
  • Before authoring `--content`, read the matching XML or Markdown guide under Related skills when available, unless already read. For XML, use only documented DocxXML tags.
  • Match `--doc-format` to `--content`; for multiline content, prefer `@file` or `-` (stdin).

  lark-cli skills read lark-doc/references/lark-doc-md.md

      --content string                replacement or inserted content; XML by default or Markdown when --doc-format markdown; empty with str_replace deletes match. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --doc string                    document URL or token

      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --name string           name for the copied file, up to 256 bytes
      --token string          document token or document URL; bare tokens require --type

      --url string            recommended: Lark/Feishu document URL, including wiki URLs

Risk: write

Tips:
    • The source type must match the real file type; the API rejects mismatches.
    • A wiki URL or --token with --type wiki is resolved through wiki node_by_token, then its underlying Drive resource is copied.
    • Use `--extra target_type=docx` with a legacy doc source to create the copy as a new-version docx.
    • `--folder-token my_space` resolves the caller's My Space root folder automatically; resolution needs the drive:drive.metadata:readonly (or drive:drive) scope.
    • In bot mode, the CLI also tries to grant the current CLI user full_access on the new copy; the outcome is reported in the permission_grant output field.

commands.description: One-way file-level mirror of a Drive folder onto a local directory (Drive → local)
commands.details:
One-way file-level mirror of a Drive folder onto a local directory (Drive → local)

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +pull [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                    identity type: user | bot
      --delete-local                 delete local regular files absent from Drive (file-level mirror; empty directories are NOT pruned); requires --yes
      --dry-run                      print request without executing
      --folder-token string          source Drive folder token
      --format string                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                         help for +pull
      --if-exists string             policy when a local file already exists (skip = never touch existing files; smart = skip when local mtime is already up to date; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "overwrite")
  -q, --jq string                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                         shorthand for --format json
      --local-dir string             local root directory (relative to cwd)
      --on-duplicate-remote string   policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|rename|newest|oldest) (default "fail")
      --yes                          confirm --delete-local before deleting local files

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Only entries with type=file are downloaded; online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides) and shortcuts are skipped.
    • Subfolders recurse and are reproduced as local directories under --local-dir; missing parents are created automatically.
    • For repeat syncs, --if-exists=smart is the recommended best-effort incremental mode: it compares local mtime with Drive modified_time and skips downloads when the local copy is already up to date.
    • Duplicate remote rel_path conflicts fail by default. Use --on-duplicate-remote=rename to download duplicate files with stable hashed suffixes.
    • --delete-local requires --yes; without --yes the command is rejected upfront so a stray flag never deletes anything.

delete-local.description: delete local regular files absent from Drive (file-level mirror; empty directories are NOT pruned); requires --yes

if-exists.description: policy when a local file already exists (skip = never touch existing files; smart = skip when local mtime is already up to date; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "overwrite")

on-duplicate-remote.description: policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|rename|newest|oldest) (default "fail")

commands.description: File-level mirror of a local directory onto a Drive folder (local → Drive; remote-only directories are not removed)
commands.details:
File-level mirror of a local directory onto a Drive folder (local → Drive; remote-only directories are not removed)

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +push [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                    identity type: user | bot
      --delete-remote                delete Drive files absent locally (file-level mirror; remote-only directories are not removed); requires --yes
      --dry-run                      print request without executing
      --folder-token string          target Drive folder token
      --format string                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                         help for +push
      --if-exists string             policy when a Drive file already exists at the same rel_path (skip = never touch existing remote files; smart = skip when remote modified_time already matches or is newer, otherwise fall through to overwrite semantics; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "skip")
  -q, --jq string                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                         shorthand for --format json
      --local-dir string             local root directory (relative to cwd)
      --on-duplicate-remote string   policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")
      --yes                          confirm --delete-remote before deleting Drive files

Risk: write

Tips:
    • This is a file-level mirror: only type=file entries are uploaded, overwritten or deleted. Online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides), shortcuts, and remote-only directories are never touched.
    • Local directory structure (including empty directories) is mirrored to Drive via create_folder; existing remote folders are reused.
    • For repeat syncs, --if-exists=smart is a best-effort incremental mode: it compares local mtime with Drive modified_time and skips uploads when the remote copy is already up to date; otherwise it falls through to the same overwrite path as --if-exists=overwrite.
    • Duplicate remote rel_path conflicts fail by default before upload, overwrite, or delete. Use --on-duplicate-remote=newest|oldest only when the conflict is duplicate files and you explicitly want to target one.
    • Default --if-exists=skip is the safe choice while the upload_all overwrite-version field is rolling out. Pass --if-exists=overwrite to replace remote bytes; on tenants without the field it surfaces a structured api_error and the run exits non-zero. The same caveat applies when --if-exists=smart decides the remote file is older and falls through to overwrite.
    • --delete-remote requires --yes; without --yes the command is rejected upfront so a stray flag never deletes anything.
    • --delete-remote --yes also requires the space:document:delete scope. Validate runs a dynamic pre-flight check when the flag is on, so a missing grant fails the run before any upload — preventing a half-synced state where files were uploaded but the cleanup pass cannot delete.
    • Item-level failures (upload, overwrite, folder, delete) bump summary.failed and the run exits non-zero. If any upload or folder step fails, the --delete-remote phase is skipped entirely so a partial upload never triggers remote deletion.

delete-remote.description: delete Drive files absent locally (file-level mirror; remote-only directories are not removed); requires --yes

if-exists.description: policy when a Drive file already exists at the same rel_path (skip = never touch existing remote files; smart = skip when remote modified_time already matches or is newer, otherwise fall through to overwrite semantics; overwrite = always replace) (overwrite|smart|skip) (default "skip")

on-duplicate-remote.description: policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")

Risk: read

Tips:
    • Only entries with type=file are compared; online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides) and shortcuts are skipped.
    • Default detection=exact downloads files present on both sides and SHA-256 hashes them in memory; expect noticeable I/O on large folders.
    • Pass --quick for the recommended fast preflight mode: it compares local mtime with Drive modified_time, skips remote downloads, and reports detection=quick as a best-effort diff.

commands.description: Two-way sync between a local directory and a Drive folder
commands.details:
Two-way sync between a local directory and a Drive folder

Usage:
  lark-cli drive +sync [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                    identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                      print request without executing
      --folder-token string          Drive folder token
      --format string                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                         help for +sync
  -q, --jq string                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                         shorthand for --format json
      --local-dir string             local root directory (relative to cwd)
      --on-conflict string           conflict resolution when both sides modified a file (local-wins|remote-wins|keep-both|ask) (default "remote-wins")
      --on-duplicate-remote string   policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")
      --quick                        use best-effort modified_time comparison instead of SHA-256 hash; mismatched timestamps can still trigger real sync writes

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Two-way sync: new remote files are pulled, new local files are pushed, and conflicts (both sides modified) are resolved by --on-conflict.
    • Default --on-conflict=remote-wins pulls the remote version when both sides changed a file. Use local-wins to push instead, keep-both to rename and keep both copies, or ask for interactive resolution.
    • Pass --quick for faster best-effort diff detection using modified_time instead of SHA-256 hash (no remote file downloads needed during diffing).
    • Because +sync acts on the diff, --quick can still pull, overwrite, or rename files when timestamps differ even if file contents are actually unchanged.
    • Actual sync execution pre-flights download, upload, and folder-create scopes before listing or walking, so missing grants fail before any partial sync can start.
    • Only entries with type=file are synced; online docs (docx, sheet, bitable, mindnote, slides) and shortcuts are skipped.

on-conflict.description: conflict resolution when both sides modified a file (local-wins|remote-wins|keep-both|ask) (default "remote-wins")

on-duplicate-remote.description: policy when multiple remote Drive entries map to the same rel_path (fail|newest|oldest) (default "fail")

quick.description: use best-effort modified_time comparison instead of SHA-256 hash; mismatched timestamps can still trigger real sync writes

      --as string                      identity type: user | bot

  -h, --help                           help for +update-title
  -q, --jq string                      jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                           shorthand for --format json
      --on-extension-mismatch string   --type file only: keep appends the current extension when the title has none and rejects a different extension; allow submits the title verbatim without reading the current title (keep|allow) (default "keep")
      --title string                   new title to set; must not be empty
      --token string                   target token or URL; bare tokens require --type
      --type string                    target type for bare --token; optional for URLs but must match the URL type when provided (docx|sheet|bitable|base|slides|file|folder|wiki|apps|doc|mindnote)
      --url string                     recommended: Lark/Feishu URL of the target (docx/sheets/base/slides/file/folder/wiki)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • --type must match the real resource type; a mismatched type fails with 981003 not found, the same code an unknown token returns.
    • For a wiki node pass the node token from the /wiki/ URL with --type wiki; the underlying document token is not accepted there. Renaming either side keeps node and document titles in sync.
    • For --type file the title replaces the whole file name, extension included. By default the CLI reads the current name and appends its extension when the title has none, reporting it in the extension_appended output field; a title that changes the extension is rejected unless --on-extension-mismatch=allow.
    • An empty title is rejected locally; the API would accept it and leave the resource with a blank title.
    • Renames are rate limited (99991400): serialize bulk renames instead of running them in parallel, and retry later with exponential backoff.
    • 981004 forbidden means the identity lacks edit permission on the target, not a missing scope; the scope codes are 99991672 (app scope not applied) and 99991679 (user did not grant it).

commands.description: Use when updating an existing mail draft without sending it. Prefer this shortcut over calling raw drafts.get or drafts.update directly, because it performs draft-safe MIME read/patch/write editing while preserving unchanged structure, attachments, and headers where possible.
commands.details:
Use when updating an existing mail draft without sending it. Prefer this shortcut over calling raw drafts.get or drafts.update directly, because it performs draft-safe MIME read/patch/write editing while preserving unchanged structure, attachments, and headers where possible.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +draft-edit [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                   identity type: user
      --body string                 Full email body for a complete replacement (set_body). Prefer HTML for rich formatting (bold, lists, links); plain text is also supported. Body type is auto-detected. Use --patch-file with set_reply_body when you need to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block; use --body when you want a full body replacement. Mutually exclusive with --body-file. Cannot be combined with --patch-file body ops.
      --body-file string            Path (relative, within cwd subtree) to a file containing the email body HTML. Mutually exclusive with --body. Size capped at 32 MB. (supports @file)
      --draft-id string             Target draft ID. Required for real edits. It can be omitted only when using the --print-patch-template flag by itself.
      --dry-run                     print request without executing
      --format string               output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
      --from string                 Mailbox email address containing the draft (default: me). Prefer --mailbox for clarity; --from is kept for backward compatibility. (default "me")
  -h, --help                        help for +draft-edit
      --inspect                     Inspect the draft without modifying it. Returns the draft projection including subject, recipients, body summary, has_quoted_content (whether the draft contains a reply/forward quote block), attachments_summary (with part_id and cid for each attachment), and inline_summary. Run this BEFORE editing body to check has_quoted_content: if true, use set_reply_body in --patch-file to preserve the quote; if false, use set_body.
  -q, --jq string                   jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                        shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string              Mailbox email address that owns the draft (default: falls back to --from, then me). Takes priority over --from when both are set.
      --patch-file string           Advanced edit entry point for body edits, incremental recipient changes, header edits, attachment changes, or inline-image changes. Use --body/--body-file for quick full-body replacement; use --patch-file with set_body/set_reply_body when you need typed body ops, especially set_reply_body to preserve an existing reply/forward quote block. Run --inspect first to check has_quoted_content, then --print-patch-template for the JSON structure. Relative path only.
      --print-patch-template        Print the JSON template and supported operations for the --patch-file flag. Recommended first step before generating a patch file. No draft read or write is performed.
      --remove-event                Remove the calendar event from the draft.
      --request-receipt             Request a read receipt (Message Disposition Notification, RFC 3798) addressed to the draft's sender. Recipient mail clients may prompt the user, send automatically, or silently ignore — delivery of a receipt is not guaranteed. Adds the Disposition-Notification-To header; existing value is overwritten.
      --set-bcc string              Replace the entire Bcc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --set-cc string               Replace the entire Cc recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --set-event-end string        Set calendar event end time (ISO 8601).
      --set-event-location string   Set calendar event location.
      --set-event-start string      Set calendar event start time (ISO 8601).
      --set-event-summary string    Set calendar event title. Must be used together with --set-event-start and --set-event-end.
      --set-priority string         Set email priority: high, normal, low. Setting 'normal' removes any existing priority header.
      --set-subject string          Replace the subject with this final value. Use this for full subject replacement, not for appending a fragment to the existing subject.
      --set-to string               Replace the entire To recipient list with the addresses provided here. Separate multiple addresses with commas. Display-name format is supported.
      --show-lint-details           Include lint metadata (lint_applied[] / original_blocked[]) in the envelope. Default: no lint fields are returned to keep the envelope small.

Risk: write

inline.description: Inline image as one JSON object. Repeat --inline once per image; quote each value. Example value: '{"cid":"","file_path":""}'. file_path must be relative. Reference it from HTML as . CID must be unique, e.g. a random hex string. Cannot be used with --plain-text.

priority.description: Email priority: high, normal, low. If omitted, no priority header is set.

remove.description: Address to exclude from the outgoing reply. Repeat --remove once per address; quote each value.

request-receipt.description: Request a read receipt (Message Disposition Notification, RFC 3798) addressed to the sender. Recipient mail clients may prompt the user, send automatically, or silently ignore — delivery of a receipt is not guaranteed.

show-lint-details.description: Include lint metadata (lint_applied[] / original_blocked[]) in the envelope. Default: no lint fields are returned to keep the envelope small.

subject.description: Optional. Override the auto-generated Re: subject. When set, the shortcut uses this value verbatim instead of prefixing the original subject.

template-id.description: Optional. Apply a saved template by ID (decimal integer string) before composing. The template's body/to/cc/bcc/attachments are appended to the reply-derived values (no de-duplication; see warning in Execute output).

to.description: Additional To address. Repeat --to once per recipient; quote each value; appended to original recipients.

commands.description: Update an existing mail template. Supports --inspect (read-only projection), --print-patch-template (prints a JSON skeleton for --patch-file), and flat flags (--set-subject / --set-name / etc). Internally it GETs the template, applies the patch, rewrites local paths to cid: refs, and PUTs a full-replace update (no optimistic locking: last-write-wins).

commands.description: Use when querying a full mail conversation/thread by thread ID. Returns all messages in chronological order, including replies and drafts, with body content and attachments metadata, including inline images.
commands.details:
Use when querying a full mail conversation/thread by thread ID. Returns all messages in chronological order, including replies and drafts, with body content and attachments metadata, including inline images.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +thread [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --format string         output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                  help for +thread
      --html                  Whether to return HTML body (false returns plain text only to save bandwidth) (default true)
      --include-spam-trash    Also return messages from SPAM and TRASH folders (excluded by default)
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string        email address (default: me) (default "me")
      --print-output-schema   Print output field reference (run this first to learn field names before parsing output)
      --thread-id string      Required. Email thread ID

Risk: read

html.description: Whether to return HTML body (false returns plain text only to save bandwidth) (default true)

include-spam-trash.description: Also return messages from SPAM and TRASH folders (excluded by default)

mailbox.description: email address (default: me) (default "me")

print-output-schema.description: Print output field reference (run this first to learn field names before parsing output)

commands.description: Modify existing mail threads by adding/removing label IDs or moving them to a folder. Batches thread IDs in groups of 20 and keeps output compact.
commands.details:
Modify existing mail threads by adding/removing label IDs or moving them to a folder. Batches thread IDs in groups of 20 and keeps output compact.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +thread-modify [flags]

Flags:
      --add-folder string          Folder ID to move threads to.
      --add-label-ids strings      Label IDs to add. System labels unread/important/other/flagged are normalized to upper case.
      --as string                  identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                    print request without executing
      --format string              output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                       help for +thread-modify
  -q, --jq string                  jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                       shorthand for --format json
      --mailbox string             Mailbox email address that owns the threads (default: me). (default "me")
      --remove-label-ids strings   Label IDs to remove. Cannot overlap with --add-label-ids.
      --thread-ids stringArray     Thread IDs to modify; comma-separated or repeat the flag.

Risk: write

add-folder.description: Folder ID to move threads to.

add-label-ids.description: Label IDs to add. System labels unread/important/other/flagged are normalized to upper case.

mailbox.description: Mailbox email address that owns the threads (default: me). (default "me")

remove-label-ids.description: Label IDs to remove. Cannot overlap with --add-label-ids.

thread-ids.description: Thread IDs to modify; comma-separated or repeat the flag.

commands.description: List mail summaries (date/from/subject/message_id). Use --query for full-text search, --filter for exact-match conditions.
commands.details:
List mail summaries (date/from/subject/message_id). Use --query for full-text search, --filter for exact-match conditions.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +triage [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --filter string         exact-match condition filter (JSON or key=value). Narrow results by folder, label, sender, recipient, unread status, etc. Run --print-filter-schema to see all fields. Example: {"folder":"INBOX","from":["alice@example.com"]}
      --folder string         folder name or system folder ID filter
      --folder-id string      explicit folder ID filter
      --format string         output format: table | json | data (json/data output object with pagination fields) (table|json|data) (default "table")
  -h, --help                  help for +triage
      --is-unread             filter unread messages
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --labels                include label IDs in output
      --mailbox string        email address (default: me) (default "me")
      --max int               maximum number of messages to fetch (1-400; auto-paginates internally) (default 20)
      --page-token string     pagination token from a previous response to fetch the next page
      --print-filter-schema   print --filter field reference and exit
      --query string          full-text keyword search across from/to/subject/body (max 50 chars). Example: "budget report"

Risk: read

filter.description: exact-match condition filter (JSON or key=value). Narrow results by folder, label, sender, recipient, unread status, etc. Run --print-filter-schema to see all fields. Example: {"folder":"INBOX","from":["alice@example.com"]}

folder.description: folder name or system folder ID filter

mailbox.description: email address (default: me) (default "me")

max.description: maximum number of messages to fetch (1-400; auto-paginates internally) (default 20)

page-token.description: pagination token from a previous response to fetch the next page

query.description: full-text keyword search across from/to/subject/body (max 50 chars). Example: "budget report"

commands.description: Watch for incoming mail events via WebSocket (requires scope mail:event and bot event mail.user_mailbox.event.message_received_v1 added). Run with --print-output-schema to see per-format field reference before parsing output.
commands.details:
Watch for incoming mail events via WebSocket (requires scope mail:event and bot event mail.user_mailbox.event.message_received_v1 added). Run with --print-output-schema to see per-format field reference before parsing output.

Usage:
  lark-cli mail +watch [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --folder-ids string     filter: folder IDs JSON array, e.g. ["INBOX","SENT"]
      --folders string        filter: folder names JSON array, e.g. ["inbox","news"]
      --format string         json: NDJSON stream with ok/data envelope; data: bare NDJSON stream (json|data) (default "data")
  -h, --help                  help for +watch
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --label-ids string      filter: label IDs JSON array, e.g. ["FLAGGED","IMPORTANT"]
      --labels string         filter: label names JSON array, e.g. ["important","team-label"]
      --mailbox string        email address (default: me) (default "me")
      --msg-format string     message payload mode: metadata(headers + meta, for triage/notification) | minimal(IDs and state only, no headers, for tracking read/folder changes) | plain_text_full(all metadata fields + full plain-text body) | event(raw WebSocket event, no API call, for debug) | full(full message including HTML body and attachments) (default "metadata")
      --output-dir string     Write each message as a JSON file (always full payload, regardless of --msg-format)
      --print-output-schema   Print output field reference per --msg-format (run this first to learn field names before parsing output)

Risk: read

folder-ids.description: filter: folder IDs JSON array, e.g. ["INBOX","SENT"]

folders.description: filter: folder names JSON array, e.g. ["inbox","news"]

label-ids.description: filter: label IDs JSON array, e.g. ["FLAGGED","IMPORTANT"]

labels.description: filter: label names JSON array, e.g. ["important","team-label"]

mailbox.description: email address (default: me) (default "me")

msg-format.description: message payload mode: metadata(headers + meta, for triage/notification) | minimal(IDs and state only, no headers, for tracking read/folder changes) | plain_text_full(all metadata fields + full plain-text body) | event(raw WebSocket event, no API call, for debug) | full(full message including HTML body and attachments) (default "metadata")

output-dir.description: Write each message as a JSON file (always full payload, regardless of --msg-format)

print-output-schema.description: Print output field reference per --msg-format (run this first to learn field names before parsing output)

commands.description: Create a Markdown file in Drive
commands.details:
Create a Markdown file in Drive

Usage:
  lark-cli markdown +create [flags]

Flags:
      --as string             identity type: user | bot
      --content string        Markdown content (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --dry-run               print request without executing
      --file string           local .md file path
      --folder-token string   target Drive folder token (default: root folder; mutually exclusive with --wiki-token)
      --format string         output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                  help for +create
  -q, --jq string             jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                  shorthand for --format json
      --name string           file name with .md suffix; required with --content, optional with --file
      --wiki-token string     target wiki node token (uploads under that wiki node; mutually exclusive with --folder-token)

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Omit both --folder-token and --wiki-token to create the Markdown file in the caller's Drive root folder.
    • Use --wiki-token <wiki_node_token> to create the Markdown file under a wiki node; the shortcut maps this to parent_type=wiki automatically.
    • --folder-token and --wiki-token also accept full Lark URLs and normalize them to the required token.

folder-token.description: target Drive folder token (default: root folder; mutually exclusive with --wiki-token)

name.description: file name with .md suffix; required with --content, optional with --file

wiki-token.description: target wiki node token (uploads under that wiki node; mutually exclusive with --folder-token)

Replace the AI summary of a minute

When to use:
  • Replace the minute's AI summary text in full.

Prerequisites:
  • Prefer reading the current summary via `+detail` with `--summary` before overwriting

commands.description: Add, update, or delete todo item(s) on a minute
commands.details:
Add, update, or delete todo item(s) on a minute

Risk: write

When to use:
  • Write AI todos that live inside a minute — not Lark Task list items.

Avoid when:
  • Personal or shared Task lists → use the task domain (`lark-cli task`), not this shortcut

Prerequisites:
  • `minute_token` from `+search`, a minutes URL, or VC recording
  • For update/delete: `todo_id` from `+detail` with `--todo`

Tips:
  • Single todo: `--operation add --todo "..." --is-done=false`.
  • Batch: `--todos '[{"operation":"add","content":"...","is_done":false}, ...]'` or `--todos @todos.json`.
  • Batch can mix add, update, and delete in one request; array order is preserved in the API body.
  • Update: `--operation update --todo-id <id> --todo "..." --is-done`.
  • Delete: `--operation delete --todo-id <id>`.
  • `content` is plain text only; markdown formatting is not supported.
  • Use `lark-cli minutes +detail --minute-tokens <token> --todo` to read current todos before writing.

Examples:
  • Add one unfinished todo
      lark-cli minutes +todo --minute-token obcnxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx --operation add --todo "跟进预算审批" --is-done=false --as user

commands.description: Execute a batch of write shortcuts in one request; fail-fast on the first failing sub-op (already-applied sub-ops are NOT rolled back).
commands.details:
Execute a batch of write shortcuts in one request; fail-fast on the first failing sub-op (already-applied sub-ops are NOT rolled back).

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +batch-update [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                  identity type: user | bot
      --continue-on-error          Continue with remaining operations when a sub-operation fails; default false (abort on first failure)
      --dry-run                    print request without executing
      --flag-name string           flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string              output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                       help for +batch-update
  -q, --jq string                  jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                       shorthand for --format json
      --operations string          (required) JSON array: [{"shortcut":"+xxx-yyy","input":{...}}, ...]. shortcut uses CLI names; input is that shortcut's flag set — it includes the per-operation sheet locator (sheet_id or sheet_name) but not the spreadsheet token/url (pass that once at the top level via --url/--spreadsheet-token; +batch-update has no top-level --sheet-id). input keys are the shortcut's flags flattened into JSON (e.g. "range":"A11:B12"), not another nested layer. For basic flags use lark-cli sheets <shortcut> --help; for composite JSON flags use --print-schema --flag-name <flag>. Do not pass an explicit operation field. Fail-fast by default: the first failure aborts the remaining operations. Whether earlier sub-operations persisted is NOT uniform: pure cell/structure writes are only buffered and are dropped on failure (effective rollback), while chart/pivot-type sub-operations flush the buffered writes to disk before creating the object and cannot be rolled back. After a failure, assume neither full-rollback nor full-persist — check results, read back the current state (dims / target cells / object lists) to determine what actually applied, then resend only the unapplied part. Pass --continue-on-error to keep going past failures with successes preserved; no nesting; executed serially. (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --print-schema               print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --spreadsheet-token string   Spreadsheet locator (independent from per-operation sheet locator)
      --url string                 Spreadsheet locator (independent from per-operation sheet locator)
      --yes                        confirm high-risk operation

Risk: high-risk-write

Tips:
    • high-risk-write: preview with --dry-run, get the user's explicit consent, then re-run with --yes appended — do not pass --yes before the user has confirmed (without it the call exits 10 asking for confirmation).
    • Execution is fail-fast, NOT transactional: on "N succeeded, M failed" the succeeded sub-ops stay applied (no rollback) — fix the failure and resend ONLY the operations from the first failed index onward; resending the whole batch re-applies the succeeded ones. Pass --continue-on-error to keep going past failures instead.
    • Each sub-op is {shortcut, input}. Do NOT pass input.operation (implied by shortcut name). Repeated input.excel_id / input.spreadsheet_token / input.url fields are ignored; the top-level locator wins.
    • Chart operations are supported, but prefer +batch-chart-create / +batch-chart-update for chart-only work because their contracts and partial-failure recovery are simpler.

Passing 0 means "no cap of my own" and resolves to the same ceiling as leaving the flag alone (500000, or the offload limit with --output-path) — never down to the tool's smaller omitted-value fallback. commands.details:
Write values / formulas / styles / comments / data validation / embed-image to a cell range.

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +cells-set [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-overwrite                              Allow overwriting non-empty cells (default true); set false to error if any target cell is non-empty (default true)
      --as string                                    identity type: user | bot
      --cells [[{cell},...],...]                     JSON 2D array [[{cell},...],...], dimensions must match `--range`; each cell may carry `value` / `formula` / `multiple_values` / `cell_styles` / `note` / `rich_text` (incl. `type="embed-image"` in-cell image). To write selected values into a multi-select dropdown cell, use `multiple_values:[{"value":...}]`; do not join multiple options with commas into one `value`. Run `--print-schema` for full fields (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))
      --copy-to-range string                         Copy-to range (A1 notation): replicate what --cells wrote into --range (values/formulas/styles, per the fields actually passed) to this range; formula refs auto-shift (C2=B2 -> C3=B3). Write a one-row/one-block template then fill a whole column/area. Supports full rows '3:6', full columns 'C:E', to-col-end 'D3:D', to-row-end 'D3:3', and comma-separated multiple targets like 'C1:D2,E5:F6'.
      --dry-run                                      print request without executing
      --flag-name string                             flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string                                output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                                         help for +cells-set
  -q, --jq string                                    jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                                         shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema                                 print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --range --writes                               Write range (A1 notation). XOR with --writes (single region: --range+--cells; multiple regions: --writes)
      --sheet-id --sheet-name                        Sheet reference_id — required: pass this or --sheet-name (exactly one of the two); not accepted with `--writes` (each writes item carries its own sheet selector)
      --sheet-name --sheet-id                        Sheet name — required: pass this or --sheet-id (exactly one of the two); not accepted with `--writes` (each writes item carries its own sheet selector)
      --spreadsheet-token --url                      Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --url --spreadsheet-token                      Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)
      --writes {sheet_name|sheet_id, range, cells}   Multi-region write as a JSON array (up to 100 items), each {sheet_name|sheet_id, range, cells} — the sheet selector LIVES IN EACH ITEM (same convention as +batch-update sub-ops and +styles-put items; the top-level --sheet-name is rejected). cells has the same shape as `--cells` (2D array; per-cell cell_styles/border_styles allowed). The whole array goes out as ONE batched request (fail-fast; read back to confirm what applied before resending), cross-sheet supported; typical use: fixing formulas scattered across ranges/sheets — do not assemble a +batch-update operations array for this. XOR with `--range`+`--cells`; range-level uniform styling stays with +styles-put afterwards (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Example: lark-cli sheets +cells-set --url <URL> --sheet-name Sheet1 --range A1:B1 --cells '[[{"value":"名称"},{"formula":"=SUM(B2:B9)"}]]'
    • --cells is always a 2D array (rows × cells), even for one cell: [[{"value":…}]].
    • Scattered regions (e.g. fixing formulas across ranges/sheets): --writes '[{"sheet_name":…,"range":…,"cells":[[…]]}, …]' — one batch request (fail-fast, no rollback), sheet selector inside each item.

commands.details:
Resize columns in pixels (NOT Excel char units): --range + --width <px> for one uniform width, --widths '{"A":100,"C:E":120}' for per-column widths in one batch request, or --type standard to reset (--range is column letters like "A:E" or "C"; no auto for cols).

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets +cols-resize [flags]

Flags:
      --as string                 identity type: user | bot
      --dry-run                   print request without executing
      --flag-name string          flag whose schema to print (omit to list introspectable flags); used with --print-schema
      --format string             output format: json (default) | pretty | table | ndjson | csv (default "json")
  -h, --help                      help for +cols-resize
  -q, --jq string                 jq expression to filter JSON output
      --json                      shorthand for --format json
      --print-schema              print JSON Schema for a composite flag instead of executing
      --range A:E                 Column closed range to resize; column letters like A:E or `C` (single column). Required for the uniform form (with `--width` or `--type`); omit with the map form (`--widths`)
      --sheet-id --sheet-name     Sheet reference_id — required: pass this or --sheet-name (exactly one of the two)
      --sheet-name --sheet-id     Sheet name — required: pass this or --sheet-id (exactly one of the two)
      --spreadsheet-token --url   Spreadsheet token (XOR with --url)
      --type pixel                Sizing mode: pixel (requires `--width`) / `standard` (reset to default column width). Passing --width alone is the common form; `--type standard` cannot be combined with `--width` (pixel|standard)
      --url --spreadsheet-token   Spreadsheet URL (XOR with --spreadsheet-token)
      --width --range             Uniform column width in pixels (e.g. 80 / 120 / 200; NOT Excel character units), used with --range. Passing --width implies pixel mode; --type may be omitted (or set to `pixel` — equivalent). For per-column widths use `--widths`
      --widths "A"                Per-column width map — set different widths for many columns in one batched call (fail-fast; read back before resending). Keys: single column ("A") or closed range (`"C:E"`); values: pixel width (e.g. 80 / 120 / 200) or `"standard"` (reset to default). Units are pixels, NOT Excel character units (px ≈ chars × 8 + 16). Mutually exclusive with `--range` / `--width` / `--type` (supports @file, - reads stdin (one flag per call; use @file for others))

Risk: write

Tips:
    • Example: lark-cli sheets +cols-resize --url <URL> --sheet-name Sheet1 --range A:C --width 120
    • Different widths per column in one batch request: --widths '{"A":80,"C:E":120}'. Widths are pixels (px ≈ chars × 8 + 16), not Excel character units.

For a full untruncated read, use --output-path to dump to a file (the cap auto-raises to a bounded 20M chars — the read path is not streaming, this cap is the memory guard; pass an explicit --max-chars for more); only lower it (e.g. 25000) when you want results inline without a file, paging via has_more. Passing 0 means "no cap of my own" and resolves to the same ceiling as leaving the flag alone (500000, or the offload limit with --output-path) — never down to the tool's smaller omitted-value fallback. (default 500000)

The stdout receipt reports `complete` (and `truncated` plus a warning when the cap was hit), so check it instead of assuming the file holds the whole sheet. Note the file is the data payload as JSON — on +csv-get too, where the CSV text sits in a field inside it — not a ready-to-use .csv; redirect stdout instead if you want a bare CSV file. Omit it to print to stdout as usual.
